chunks: All goodness has been gathered in three qualities: looking, silence, and speech. Every glance that contains no reflection is heedlessness, every speech that contains no dhikr is idle talk, and every silence that contains no thought is neglect. So blessed is the one whose gaze is reflective, whose silence is thoughtful, whose speech is dhikr, who weeps over his sin, and from whose harm people are safe.

key_terms.اعْتِبَارٌ: reflection that draws a lesson from what one sees
key_terms.شَرَّهُ: his harm or evil toward others
key_terms.لَغْوٌ: vain or idle speech without benefit

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali عليه السلام teach about reflective speech, silence, and character?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that moral excellence is concentrated in how a person sees, remains silent, and speaks. Imam Ali عليه السلام defines true virtue as reflective perception, contemplative silence, and speech filled with dhikr, joined with repentance and harmlessness toward others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5876 - Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said:

"All goodness has been gathered in three qualities: looking, silence, and speech.
Every glance that lacks reflection is heedlessness, every speech without the remembrance (of Allah (swt)) is idle talk, and every silence without contemplation is neglect.
Glad tidings are for the one whose gaze is reflective, whose silence is thoughtful, whose speech is in remembrance, who weeps over his sins, and from whose harm people are safe."
